statusDetail: Coverage-complete agentic audit of five representative public paths. Authenticated account management, subscription checkout completion and video playback were not exercised because they require credentials/payment or media-session scope; applicable checks were judged from the exposed entry states.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to the light capture; the consent surface remains white and platform metadata reports color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface and text tokens.

findings.summary: A full-viewport consent-or-pay wall obscures all editorial content on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, article, section, search and 404 screenshots all open on the same blocking privacy dialog rather than the requested content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface with equally direct accept/reject controls and preserve immediate access to core content.

findings.summary: The blocking consent overlay uses a custom role=dialog surface rather than a native dialog with platform dismissal semantics.
findings.evidence: DOM recon found one [role=dialog] and zero native dialog elements; the full-screen overlay has no visible close or reject control.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog only where modality is necessary, provide an explicit close/reject action, and use declarative platform controls.

findings.summary: First-load chrome occupies the entire viewport and displaces the requested content.
findings.evidence: At 360×800 the screenshot contains only consent copy and controls; no headline or article content is visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the privacy UI to the minimum information and controls needed at decision time, with details available on demand.

findings.summary: Repeated teaser components do not expose component-level container responsiveness.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero elements with a non-normal container-type across a page with many teaser cards reused in multiple widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable teaser/card wrappers containment and adapt internals with container queries where their placement changes.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on sampled controls.
findings.evidence: The focus probe programmatically focused skip links, header controls and story links; all sampled computed outlines were “none”.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible indicator with sufficient contrast, preserving native outlines unless an equivalent is supplied.

findings.summary: The primary reading journey is blocked before users can reach the requested story.
findings.evidence: Every fresh article and section visit is covered by the consent-or-pay wall; the only non-tracking choice shown is a paid subscription.
findings.suggestedFix: Let users continue to editorial content with a clear non-tracking choice that does not require purchase.

findings.summary: Measured load performance and visual stability are outside good Core Web Vitals ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 7.4 s and CLS 0.964 with a performance score of 0.44; the independent trace measured LCP 3.21 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset/content, reserve late content space, and defer non-critical scripts; verify with lab and field CWV.

findings.summary: The page shifts substantially during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.964 and identified layout-shift culprits; all 70 inspected images lacked width and height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image and injected-content space with width/height or aspect-ratio and stabilise consent/ad slots.

findings.summary: The critical delivery path is delayed by a large request graph and candidate blocking resources.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 112 requests and 1.18 MB transferred, including 72 scripts; the trace measured LCP 3.21 s and HAR identified a parser stylesheet plus scripts requiring deferral review.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep only essential critical CSS, confirm module/defer attributes, pre-prioritise the LCP resource, and delay consent/ad code.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 108 KiB unused JavaScript and 43 KiB unused CSS; HAR recorded 72 script requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Split template-specific code, remove unused tracker/ad modules, and ship only CSS needed by the current archetype.

findings.summary: At least one content image has no alternative text.
findings.evidence: The images primitive inspected 70 images and reported one missing alt; many others use the placeholder “Kein alternativer Text für dieses Bild vorhanden”.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide meaningful editorial alt text, or alt="" for decorative imagery; do not expose placeholder failure text.

findings.summary: Heading structure skips levels and keyboard focus is not visible.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order for multiple h4 teaser headlines; the focus probe found no visible computed outline on sampled links and buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a logical heading hierarchy and a consistent, high-contrast :focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: The page logs browser errors during a normal load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported failed/401 FedCM account-list fetches from the page and failed the console-errors audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid initiating unavailable identity-provider fetches and handle expected failures without noisy console errors.

findings.summary: Image sizing and aspect-ratio hygiene is weak.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 70/70 images without width and height; Lighthouse failed image-aspect-ratio on teaser images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width and height for every image and keep CSS object sizing consistent with the delivered crop.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP settings weaken otherwise secure transport.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found CSP with unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; the cookies primitive found 9 of 10 cookies without Secure and widespread SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on all HTTPS cookies, tighten SameSite scope, and migrate inline/eval code to nonce/hash-based CSP.

findings.summary: The initial page has a large third-party and tracking footprint before a clear choice is completed.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 75 third-party requests and 563 KB third-party transfer; tracker recon saw 21 third-party origins and long-lived analytics identifiers were already present.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not load non-essential analytics/ad/identity dependencies before consent; minimise vendors, identifiers, retention and request volume.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced XSS defenses are weakened by permissive script policy.
findings.evidence: CSP allows both unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval. HSTS, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy and a limited Permissions-Policy were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt nonce/hash-based script-src, remove unsafe-eval, and expand Permissions-Policy to the capabilities actually denied.

findings.summary: The consent choice is asymmetric: tracking is one click, while the visible non-tracking route requires payment.
findings.evidence: The first-load screenshot presents “ALLE AKZEPTIEREN” as the prominent filled control; the alternative shown is a €3.99/month WELT Pur subscription, with rejection buried under settings.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer an equally prominent reject/non-tracking choice and separate privacy consent from subscription conversion.

findings.summary: A subscription upsell is embedded in the mandatory privacy gate.
findings.evidence: The blocking dialog makes purchase the visible path to use without tracking, before users can inspect requested content.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep consent and subscription decisions separate; show commitments and cancellation terms in the optional purchase flow.

findings.summary: Responsive image delivery lacks explicit intrinsic and source-set metadata.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found all 70 images missing width/height and srcset, with four below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit responsive srcset/sizes and dimensions, and lazy-load below-fold imagery while preserving LCP priority.

findings.summary: The initial load performs disproportionate script and third-party work for a news listing.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 72 scripts and 75 third-party requests; Lighthouse identified 108 KiB unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load advertising, identity and analytics modules only after need/consent and remove unused bundles.

findings.summary: Third-party code consumes nearly half of initial transferred bytes.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 563,459 third-party bytes of 1,182,545 total, across 75 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, defer vendors until value is requested, and remove redundant identity/tracking dependencies.

findings.summary: The homepage has a large initial DOM/heap footprint for a news listing.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contained 437,912 heap nodes, 1,676,554 edges and 24.6 MB self size before extended reading.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualise or defer deep below-fold modules and reduce retained DOM/component and vendor state.

taskList.title: Replace the blocking consent-or-pay gate with a compact, equally weighted accept/reject choice, and keep subscription conversion separate.
Block non-essential third parties until consent, minimise vendors and identifiers, secure cookies, and tighten CSP.
Improve LCP and CLS by reserving late content space, prioritising the LCP resource, and deferring non-critical scripts.
Restore logical heading order and a clear high-contrast :focus-visible indicator on all controls and links.
Remove unused bundles and conditionally load advertising, identity, and analytics modules.
Emit meaningful alt text, intrinsic image dimensions, responsive srcset/sizes, and lazy loading below the fold.
Add preference-driven light and dark colour tokens and declare color-scheme.
Reduce the retained homepage DOM and vendor state by deferring deep below-fold modules.
Use component containment and container queries for reused teaser layouts where placement changes.
Avoid unavailable FedCM identity fetches and handle expected provider failures without console noise.
